purpose: Proves authWrappers classification: only an explicitly configured canonical wrapper that always invokes its argument may expose that argument as authentication evidence — never an arbitrary, unconfigured call, regardless of what it actually does at runtime. Also proves wrapping never changes what is required of the discovered guard (confirmed-shape/unresolved/contradicted, assurance modes).

expectedRoutes.note: LoggedAuth wraps Handler, which is not a configured authMiddleware entry.
ConditionalWrapper is not a configured authWrapper, so RequireAuth inside it is never exposed as evidence.
LoggedAuth(LoggedAuth(RequireAuth)): two literal hops of the same configured wrapper.
LoggedAuth wraps RequireRoleFactory("admin"); the factory's own canonical symbol resolves, "admin" is discarded.
LoggedAuth wraps RequireAuthContradicted, whose own control flow provably never denies — wrapping never promotes a contradicted guard to proven.
